perspective:
**Available to Angela (first-person reconstruction):**

I am Angela Hwang, an Asian woman, a hairdresser with a doctorate. Kevin Flores is my close friend since high school; he is a Latino man and works in construction. We confide in each other.

- **Coffee meeting:** I noticed Kevin seemed unhappy at work, so I invited him to coffee. He said he was “alright, just the usual grind.” I told him I was worried because he didn’t seem happy. He told me he was not happy, felt stuck and unfulfilled, and was going through the motions. I asked if he’d thought about what might make him happier or a different job/career. He said he had, but didn’t know where to start and felt overwhelmed. I offered to figure it out together and look into options. He agreed and thanked me.
- **Career-change support:** I believed Kevin was considering a career change and felt supportive/hopeful. I found job openings and a career counseling service and told him about them. He thanked me. I asked if he’d thought more. He told me he was interested in something creative, maybe design or architecture. I encouraged him to check the resources. He said he would and that my support meant a lot.
- **Career coach:** I believed he was hesitant, and I felt frustrated/worried. I arranged a meeting with a career coach. I told him I believed in him and that the coach could help. He said he appreciated it but wasn’t sure he was ready. I said a push could help and the coach could help him plan and gain confidence. He agreed to try. I promised to support him every step.
- **Progress:** I believed he was making progress and felt proud/relieved. I asked how it was going with the coach. He told me the coach was helpful, he had started online design courses, and he felt more confident. I said I was proud and asked if I could help. He said knowing I was there was enough and he’d ask if he needed anything. I said I’d always be there.
- **Celebration:** I believed he had successfully transitioned to a new career and felt happy/satisfied. I organized a small celebration party. I told him it was to celebrate his new career. He thanked me. I said he’d worked hard and come far. He said he was grateful and couldn’t have done it without me. I said he did the hard work, I was glad to be there, and we should enjoy the party. He agreed.

I do not have access to Kevin’s private thoughts or feelings beyond what he said, his MBTI type, hidden events, or narrator-only facts.
